links.outcome: Share of benchmark rubric criteria with failure modes and effect on scores when regraded
links.effect: On HealthBench Professional an LLM judge flags 29.6% of criteria as non-atomic and 65.4% as misaligned/rigid; rewriting bundled criteria shifts scores by up to 15.9 percentage points on affected conversations.
links.quote: We apply RIFT, a global rubric failure taxonomy, to two clinical benchmarks (HealthBench Professional and LiveMedBench), and find failure modes are meaningful: on HealthBench Professional an LLM judge flags 29.6% of criteria as non-atomic and 65.4% as misaligned/rigid.

unlisted_practices: Auditing grading rubrics of medical LLM benchmarks for non-atomic (bundled) and misaligned/rigid criteria using a rubric failure taxonomy

screen.reason: The paper investigates failure modes and rubric design in clinical LLM benchmark evaluation (meta-benchmarking) rather than evaluating a specific clinical deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
